guarantees: Consumes the Box without running its destructor.
Returned pointer is non-null and properly aligned.
For unsized T, the raw pointer carries the metadata needed to identify the pointee and its layout.
caller_obligations_after_return: Retain enough information to eventually destroy T and release the allocation, or intentionally leak it.
If reconstructing Box<T>, preserve the allocation/layout/value-validity requirements of Box::from_raw.
Respect the raw pointer's provenance and aliasing constraints when accessing memory.

operations.ownership_transition: The resulting Box takes ownership of the pointee/allocation and will drop T and release non-zero-sized storage through Global.
preconditions: The pointer and metadata describe memory with the Box layout for T.
For non-zero-sized values, storage was allocated by Global with the matching layout.
The pointer denotes a valid value of T.
The pointer is non-null and sufficiently aligned; for zero-sized T an aligned dangling pointer is permitted.
No independently live owner may later destroy or deallocate the same allocation; reconstructing multiple owning Boxes from the same allocation can double free.

operations.input: Box<T, A> where T: ?Sized, A: Allocator
guarantees: Consumes the Box and returns both the pointee pointer and the allocator value needed for matching cleanup.
Returned pointer is non-null and properly aligned.
caller_obligations_after_return: Preserve the returned allocator together with the pointer, or otherwise perform cleanup through the allocator that actually owns the allocation.
Destroy T exactly once and deallocate non-zero-sized storage exactly once unless intentionally leaked.

operations.input: (*mut T, A) where T: ?Sized, A: Allocator
preconditions: The pointer was allocated by the supplied allocator A when allocation is required.
The pointer/metadata have the correct Box layout and denote a valid T.
The transfer creates exactly one owning Box for the allocation.

operations.safety: into is safe; from is unsafe
operations.relationship: Same ownership/layout contract as into_raw/from_raw, with NonNull encoding the non-null pointer invariant.

operations.safety: into is safe; from is unsafe
operations.relationship: Same allocator-carrying ownership transfer as the raw-pointer allocator variants, with NonNull encoding non-nullness.

cross_cutting.zero_sized_types: Box storage need not be allocated, but the Box pointer must still be non-null and sufficiently aligned. Box destruction skips deallocation when the computed layout size is zero.
cross_cutting.dynamically_sized_types: All raw-conversion impls are defined for T: ?Sized. Pointer metadata is therefore part of the ownership/layout identity for slices and trait objects; changing metadata can change Layout::for_value_raw and can invalidate reconstruction even when the data address is unchanged.
cross_cutting.drop: Box drop first drops T (compiler-managed) and then, for non-zero layout size, deallocates through the Box's stored allocator using Layout::for_value_raw.
cross_cutting.aliasing: The pinned Box documentation says, in an explicitly non-normative section, that Box<T> follows &mut T-style uniqueness and that derived raw pointers can be invalidated by later Box mutation/move/&mut borrowing. Raw conversion implementations contain aliasing-model-specific code to make the ownership handoff valid; consumers should rely on the API contract rather than generalizing implementation comments into a complete Rust aliasing model.
cross_cutting.type_changing_roundtrip: Casting an into_raw pointer before from_raw is justified only when the destination Box type has compatible layout, metadata, validity, and ownership/deallocation requirements. Address equality alone is not sufficient.
